subject: Post-demo: NeoEra streaming load rehearsal & allowlist / test-account checklist
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chang <alyssa@neoera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: NeoEra streaming load rehearsal & allowlist / test-account checklist

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a playbook for the customer-led rehearsal: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: Validate streaming concurrency SLOs for NeoEra's real-time annotation flow (95th pct latency < 150ms p50 token at 2k concurrent streams).
- Approach: NeoEra will run customer-driven k6 rehearsal scripts against a Redwood staging endpoint during a 3-hour test window; Redwood will provide short-lived test creds and an allowlist for IPs.

Action items (proposed):
1) NeoEra to confirm preferred test window (see options below).
2) NeoEra to share the final k6 script + traffic matrix (attachments: neoera_k6_script_v2.js, neoera_test_matrix.xlsx).
3) Redwood to provision a staging model slot, provide temp API creds, and share IP ranges for allowlist.
4) Engineering handshake: Soojin will validate streaming slot config (KV cache sizing, max simultaneous request count), plus define fallback model variants for graceful degradation.
5) Commercial: Ben to confirm that this rehearsal is covered under the current POC (no extra cost) and capture any ask for follow-up SLA commitments in the deal record.

Test window options (pick one):
- Option A: Tue 2026-11-09, 09:00–12:00 PT
- Option B: Wed 2026-11-10, 18:00–21:00 PT (APAC overlap)
- Option C: Fri 2026-11-12, 01:00–04:00 PT (off-peak for NeoEra prod)

Security notes: temp creds will expire 72 hours after issuance; all requests must come from the allowlisted IPs or via the CloudInfra VPN. We will also capture request traces for the rehearsal for post-run analysis.

Please reply with your preferred window and attach the final k6 script you plan to run. If you want Redwood to run a short smoke pass first, we can do a 30-minute dry run the day prior.

Thanks —
Chloe Martin
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: neoera_k6_script_v2.js (script), neoera_test_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alyssa Chang <alyssa@neoera.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: NeoEra Engineering <eng@neoera.com>, CloudInfra Ops <ops@cloudinfra.io>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NeoEra streaming load rehearsal & allowlist / test-account checklist

Chloe — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifying Qs.

Preferred window: Option A (2026-11-09, 09:00–12:00 PT). Our engineering team prefers daytime run for visibility.

We attached the k6 script and an updated traffic matrix (minor tweak on user ramp). Couple of asks:
- Can you confirm token-level streaming limits? We plan ~2,000 concurrent streaming sessions where each session streams intermittently (bursts of tokens, not constant).
- For the allowlist, we will provide a fixed CIDR per test machine; is /28 acceptable?
- We’d like Redwood to do the 30-minute smoke pass on 2026-11-08 at 10:00 PT.

We will loop in internal SRE (ops@cloudinfra.io) to coordinate network allowlist and any VPN reachability checks.

Best,
Alyssa
Director, Platform Engineering
NeoEra

Attachments: neoera_k6_script_v2.js (script, updated), neoera_test_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, v3)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chang <alyssa@neoera.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NeoEra streaming load rehearsal & allowlist / test-account checklist

Alyssa — thanks, looks good. A couple of technical clarifications and the checklist I’ll execute: 

Technical bits:
- Streaming concurrency: staging slot can sustain 2k concurrent streaming sessions if the per-session average tokens/sec stay < 18 during steady-state. If your bursts exceed that, we’ll instrument autoscaling thresholds.
- Token-level limits: we enforce a 4k-token soft cap per request in staging; long-lived sessions should page in tokens using the chunked streaming pattern in the script.
- Allowlist: /28 per test machine is fine; we prefer a small set of CIDRs (max 6) so ops can maintain the firewall rules easily.

What I will do (internal):
- Provision a staging model slot and create temp API credentials (redwood-temp-creds.txt). Creds will be created on 2026-11-06 and expire 72 hours later.
- Share the allowlist IP ranges (we’ll provide 3 CIDRs to start).
- Run a 30-minute smoke pass on 2026-11-08 10:00 PT and validate the k6 script against our streaming endpoint. I’ll capture traces and a token-latency histogram for the run.
- Configure fallback: primary model (redwood-stream-1.2) with fallback to compact-quant variant at 90% CPU/GPU utilization.

Pre-run checklist for NeoEra (please confirm):
- Final k6 script uploaded to shared Drive link.
- Test machines’ outgoing IPs (CIDR list) sent to ops@redwood.ai.
- Confirm ramp profile in the matrix (you sent v3 — we’ll use that unless you send another).

If any of the above items change, flag right away. I’ll post the temp creds and IP ranges by EOD 2026-11-06.

— Soojin
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-temp-creds.txt (will be posted), staging-slot-config.yml (internal note)
